newsitem.title: EGYPT: Rabin offered full Golan withdrawal -- Mubarak.
newsitem.headline: Rabin offered full Golan withdrawal -- Mubarak.

text.p: The late Israeli prime minister, Yitzhak Rabin, was ready for full withdrawal from the Golan Heights, Syria's main demand in peace talks, Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said in an interview published on Wednesday.

"Rabin told the U.S. administration, and he told me personally, that he was willing to withdraw from the Golan in full but he wanted to know what he would obtain in exchange," he told the London-based Arabic newspaper al-Hayat.
"He wanted normalisation and normal relations (between Israel and Syria). The man confirmed the withdrawal and this is the right way," Mubarak added.
The text of the interview was published in full in the Egyptian government newspaper al-Gomhuria.
Israel's rightwing government said on Thursday it would not be held to what it described as an "indirect" agreement by Rabin for a complete Israeli pullout from the Golan Heights.

Israel's public position was that it would discuss the extent of an Israeli withdrawal from the Golan, captured from Syria in the war of 1967, when Syria said how far it was willing to go towards normal relations with Israel.
Mubarak contrasted Rabin's position with that of rightwing Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who ousted Peres in elections in May.
"The new prime minister doesn't want to keep the commitments of the previous government. Wasn't it the government of Israel? Or the government of another state?
"Even the agreements which were signed he wants to reconsider, and this is unacceptable," Mubarak said.

"It creates deep doubts. Suppose this government makes new promises and then goes. Will the next government come and refuse to be committed to them? ... The necessary mutual trust cannot be achieved in this way."
